item.vignette: A child with severe early-onset obesity due to biallelic POMC deficiency receives setmelanotide. Hunger decreases and energy expenditure increases; skin pigmentation also becomes darker during therapy.
item.lead_in: Which receptor most directly mediates the therapeutic effect on appetite and energy balance?
item.tested_construct: Agonism of central melanocortin-4 receptors regulating hunger, satiety, and energy expenditure
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Setmelanotide is an MC4 receptor agonist. Central MC4 signaling regulates hunger, satiety, and energy expenditure; restoring this pathway can reduce food intake and promote weight loss in disorders with insufficient MC4-pathway activation. Its lesser MC1 activity explains treatment-associated pigmentation.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. MC4 receptor activation mediates the intended effects on satiety and energy balance.
distractor_explanations.B: MC1 activation contributes to increased melanin production but is not the primary therapeutic target for obesity.
distractor_explanations.C: Setmelanotide has less activity at MC3 receptors than at MC4 receptors.
distractor_explanations.D: The drug does not directly replace leptin signaling.
distractor_explanations.E: 5-HT2C agonism can reduce appetite but is not the direct target of setmelanotide.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate therapeutic MC4-receptor agonism from off-target melanocortin effects and other central appetite pathways.

item.vignette: An orally administered drug acts locally on the apical surface of intestinal epithelial cells. Fecal sodium and water increase, intestinal transit accelerates, and stool consistency softens without stimulation of chloride secretion.
item.tested_construct: Local inhibition of apical intestinal NHE3 with reduced sodium absorption
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Tenapanor locally inhibits sodium/hydrogen exchanger 3 (NHE3) on the apical surface of enterocytes. Reduced intestinal sodium absorption increases luminal water content, accelerates transit, and softens stool.

distractor_explanations.A: SGLT1 mediates sodium-coupled glucose uptake and is not the direct target of tenapanor.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Tenapanor directly inhibits apical NHE3 in the small intestine and colon.
distractor_explanations.C: NKCC transporters are not the labeled intestinal target of tenapanor.
distractor_explanations.D: CFTR activation would increase chloride secretion, which the vignette specifically excludes.
distractor_explanations.E: Basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase maintains sodium gradients but is not directly inhibited by tenapanor.

explanation.educational_objective: Link intestinal NHE3 inhibition to reduced sodium absorption, increased luminal water, and accelerated transit.

item.vignette: A topical drug used for inflammatory skin disease enters keratinocytes and activates a ligand-dependent transcription factor involved in xenobiotic sensing and epidermal homeostasis. The exact downstream therapeutic mechanism remains incompletely defined.
item.tested_construct: Agonism of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Tapinarof is an aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) agonist. AhR is a ligand-activated transcription factor; the specific mechanisms by which AhR agonism produces the therapeutic effects of topical tapinarof are not fully established.

distractor_explanations.A: Topical corticosteroids act through the glucocorticoid receptor, but tapinarof is not a corticosteroid.
distractor_explanations.B: PPAR-gamma agonism is not the labeled direct action of tapinarof.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. Tapinarof directly activates the aryl hydrocarbon receptor.
distractor_explanations.D: Vitamin D receptor agonists are used in psoriasis but represent a different mechanism.
distractor_explanations.E: Retinoic acid receptor activation is not the direct pharmacology of tapinarof.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize AhR agonism as a distinct topical anti-inflammatory pharmacologic mechanism.

item.vignette: A patient with generalized pustular psoriasis receives spesolimab-sbzo. Signaling triggered by IL-36 alpha, beta, and gamma falls, with reduced downstream inflammatory pathway activation.
item.lead_in: Which receptor is directly bound by the drug?
item.tested_construct: Monoclonal antibody binding to IL-36 receptor with blockade of IL-36 signaling
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Spesolimab-sbzo is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds IL-36 receptor (IL36R). This prevents receptor activation by IL-36 alpha, beta, and gamma and reduces downstream pro-inflammatory signaling.

distractor_explanations.A: IL-17RA blockade is a different psoriasis-directed cytokine strategy.
distractor_explanations.B: IL-23 pathway blockade is mechanistically distinct and does not explain inhibition of all three IL-36 ligands.
distractor_explanations.C: IL-4R alpha blockade targets type 2 inflammation rather than IL-36 signaling.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. Spesolimab directly binds IL36R and prevents activation by IL-36 ligands.
distractor_explanations.E: TNFR1 is not the direct target of spesolimab.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate IL-36 receptor blockade from other cytokine-targeted biologic mechanisms used in inflammatory skin disease.

item.vignette: An infant with molybdenum cofactor deficiency type A due to biallelic MOCS1 variants receives fosdenopterin. Urinary S-sulfocysteine falls after treatment.
item.lead_in: Which enzyme activity is most directly restored by formation of molybdenum cofactor from the replacement substrate?
item.tested_construct: Restoration of molybdenum-cofactor-dependent sulfite oxidase activity
item.difficulty_basis: Requires mechanistic discrimination among plausible pharmacologic targets; author estimate only.

explanation.key_explanation: Fosdenopterin provides exogenous cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate (cPMP), which is converted to molybdopterin and then molybdenum cofactor. This cofactor is required for molybdenum-dependent enzymes including sulfite oxidase, whose activity reduces neurotoxic sulfite burden and S-sulfocysteine.

distractor_explanations.A: Phenylalanine hydroxylase requires tetrahydrobiopterin rather than molybdenum cofactor.
distractor_explanations.B: Branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase requires thiamine pyrophosphate and other cofactors, not MoCo.
distractor_explanations.C: Homogentisate dioxygenase is not a molybdenum-cofactor-dependent enzyme.
distractor_explanations.D: Cystathionine beta-synthase requires pyridoxal phosphate rather than MoCo.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. Sulfite oxidase is MoCo dependent and its restoration explains the fall in toxic sulfite-derived metabolites.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect cPMP replacement in MOCS1 deficiency with restoration of molybdenum cofactor and sulfite oxidase function.
